method.formula: weighted_increase = SUM(qty x delta_jpy) / SUM(qty x bp_prior) - 1
method.recipe: price_bp_weighted_compare_pn.csv filtered to in_scope == True AND unpriced_reason IS NULL
method.why: The exchange rate and the purchase discount are both already in force, so neither is a forward move. Multiplying them into the result would add changes that are already inside today's prices. The move is measured from the price comparison instead.
method.exchange_rate_note: The rate is issued by ISZJ and applied. It is not a choice, and nothing is passed on or held back.

live_inputs.note: Recorded for traceability. None of these is an input to the weighted increase.

ebp_evidence.claim: The Export Base Price is built up from IML's own costs, and our purchase price is a discount off it.
ebp_evidence.source: Masumi Hayakawa (IML), 10 November 2025, "FW: ISZE 移転価格対応 10/30打ち合わせメモ・今後の対応事項につきまして"
ebp_evidence.detail: The factors are 62% on vehicle parts and 73.5% on industrial engines, applied to IML's Export Base Price. Worked example: an Export Base Price of 1,000 JPY gives a purchase price of 620 JPY on vehicle parts. The Export Base Price therefore sits above our purchase cost by construction, and it is not a restatement of any single cost line of ours.

ebp_evidence.claim: IML builds its offer price from supplier cost plus a target gross profit.
ebp_evidence.source: Hideya Kondou (ISZJ), 24 November 2020, "ITUK向けMMU新規ハーネスの価格設定について"
ebp_evidence.detail: Normal at 25% gross profit, Best at 17%. So the Export Base Price is a supplier cost plus a stated margin - a build-up, not a rebilling of anyone else's cost.

ebp_evidence.claim: The discount change and the base-price revision happen at the same moment.
ebp_evidence.source: Takayoshi Suzuki, 22 December 2025, "discount/whole sales ratio revisoin from Jan 5th 2026"
ebp_evidence.detail: Valid from 5 January 2026, and the mail states it is "the same timing with annual EBP revision". This is why the discount cannot be treated as a forward move: it was applied when the base price was last revised.

ebp_evidence.claim: The base price and the class letter arrive together from Japan.
ebp_evidence.source: Peeraya Sawangsaensuk (IMIT), 29 April 2026, "RE: base price class"
ebp_evidence.detail: "Please find the B/P, Price Class, and remark as detailed below." The class letter is issued with the base price, so the class factor and the base price move on the same cycle.

open_items.title: Our configuration carries only the vehicle-parts rate
open_items.detail: 03_analytics/isze_pricing/config.yaml holds J: 0.673, which is the vehicle-parts rate - 1 minus the 32.7% discount in Masumi Hayakawa's mail of 10 November 2025. The industrial-engine rate is different: 73.5% in 2025, moving to 79.7% in 2026 (1 minus 20.3%). Our configuration applies that rate to every Japan-sourced part, so an industrial-engine part is priced on the vehicle-parts rate.
open_items.action: config.yaml is left alone, exactly as it stands. Question for IML: confirm the current industrial-engine rate and which part families it covers.

open_items.title: IML states a different revision size from ours
open_items.detail: Masumi Hayakawa's mail of 10 November 2025 says the CY2026 IML base price revision has an impact of "around 3% increase for ISZE (weighted average)". We measure 5.9616% on the published recipe. These are probably different revisions or different scopes - theirs may be a purchase-cost impact over a different window.
open_items.action: Open reconciliation item, and it is left open rather than closed by choosing an explanation. Ask IML for the window, the scope and the weighting behind the 3%.

caveats: The weighted increase is measured on the price comparison itself. No exchange rate and no discount is multiplied into it.
Rows with no source label carry no source split. Their weighted increase is reported separately rather than being assigned to Japan or Thailand.
Volume and mix are held flat. This is the arithmetic of the price move, not a forecast.
